The PKGBUILD defines sources for different architectures that point to official release binaries hosted on GitHub (fluxcd/flux2). These URLs are over HTTPS and belong to the legitimate upstream project. The `sha256sums` are provided for each architecture, meaning the downloads will be verified after fetching—though even if they were marked as 'SKIP', that would not make this stage unsafe, as checksum skipping is part of normal AUR workflow and does not imply active malicious behavior during source fetch.

There is no top-level code execution outside of standard variable assignments. The `pkgver()` function is absent, so no dynamic version calculation occurs that could involve command substitution or network calls. The only executable sections (`package()`) are not sourced or run under `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, so they are out of scope for this safety gate. Sourcing this PKGBUILD and downloading the sources poses no risk of remote code execution, data exfiltration, or unintended side effects.

All operations during the specified commands are limited to secure, expected behaviors: cloning or downloading from declared sources and parsing static metadata.
</details>

The checksums are explicitly defined and match standard practice for verifying the integrity of downloaded binaries.

In the `package()` function, the binary is installed into `/usr/bin`, and shell completion scripts for bash, fish, and zsh are generated by running the `flux completion` subcommands and installing the output into appropriate system directories. This is standard behavior for CLI tools and consistent with the package description. There are no network requests, file operations, or system modifications beyond what is necessary for packaging.

No obfuscated code, dangerous commands (like `eval`, `curl|bash`, etc.), or unexpected behaviors are present. Each architecture-specific binary is fetched over HTTPS and accompanied by a matching SHA-256 checksum, ensuring integrity. While the checksums validate the expected binaries, the use of GitHub release binaries (as opposed to building from source) is typical for `-bin` packages in AUR and does not constitute a security issue by itself.

This file contains no malicious content and adheres to standard AUR packaging practices. The declared sources are verifiable and consistent with the project's release process. There are no red flags indicating supply chain compromise.

Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` and `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` on this PKGBUILD is safe. The global (top-level) scope contains only variable assignments — no command substitution, no `curl|bash`, no `eval`, no encoded payloads, and no exfiltration attempts. There is no `pkgver()` function defined; `pkgver` is a static string, so nothing executes when the PKGBUILD is sourced beyond plain variable parsing.

The `source` arrays point to the official fluxcd/flux2 GitHub releases over HTTPS, with pinned, non-SKIP sha256 checksums for all three architectures — these are exactly the kinds of standard, verifiable sources this gate is designed to fetch. The `package()` function executes the downloaded binary to generate shell completions, but `package()` is not run by either of the two commands in scope (`--nobuild` stops before `build()`/`package()`, and `--noprepare` skips `prepare()`); it will be covered in the full PKGBUILD audit. Running a package's own binary to emit completion scripts is standard packaging practice in any case.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Static PKGBUILD, pinned GitHub sources with checksums; no execution during fetch or sourcing.</summary>
</security_assessment>
